analysis:
Integration reviewed all 21 units against the replayed source. The PR scopes GPT-OSS client `stop` strings to the Harmony `final` channel. The scope is defined by `GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFix.finalChannelStopScope` (opener `<|channel|>final`, openerEnd `<|message|>`, closers `<|end|>`, `<|return|>`, `<|call|>`, `<|start|>`) and exposed via `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` and `ChatTemplateFixes.stopStringScope`. It is plumbed as follows: `EngineV2SlotFactory.swift:574`, `EngineV2Factory.makeBridge`, the `EngineV2Bridge` stored `let`, `EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift:249-250`, `EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request`, then `CBv2Request.stopStringScope`. `matchedStopSequence` replays `StopHoldback` with the same scope to report the matched stop. Other changes are documentation, tests and exhaustiveness updates: `.logprobs` cases in `JSONAnswerFormat` and `GLM5NextResponseFormat`, and a `.responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens` mapping in `InferenceErrorClassifier` to the existing non-provider-fault reason.

Security assessment: the scope only narrows where consumer-supplied stop strings can truncate output. It adds no keys, network surface, disk artifacts, logging or attestation/authorization change. Cache identity is unchanged: `cacheScope` still comes from the authenticated coordinator and the checkpoint salt is unchanged, so T-041 is unaffected. Response encryption (T-008, TB-002) is unchanged. Generation remains bounded by `max_tokens` and EOS tokens (T-010, T-029). The classifier maps to a closed-vocabulary reason with no content, so the E2E privacy constraint is preserved.

Unverified contracts (not findings): (1) three submodule pointer bumps (`libs/mlx`, `libs/mlx-swift`, `libs/mlx-swift-lm`) have no visible diff. The `CBv2StopStringScope` matcher and `StopHoldback` live in mlx-swift-lm, along with any other upstream engine, kernel or dependency changes that affect TB-007 and supply-chain integrity (T-013). (2) The coordinator's handling of the toolNoncompliance mapping for the new cut-off reason is platform-owned. (3) `.logprobs` passthrough in the GLM5 response-format withholding path could expose token-level data before validation if logprobs are requested. The risk is consumer-facing output and not a provider-adversary leak. Whether GLM requests logprobs is not shown.

No concrete regression is established. Deeper review of the submodule bumps is warranted.
